code:
$ docker network create northbridge-net

$ docker network ls
NETWORK ID     NAME               DRIVER    SCOPE
a3f8e9c1b2d4   northbridge-net    bridge    local
8f3a2b1c9d4e   bridge             bridge    local
caption: Same bridge driver as the default network -- the difference is Docker only runs its embedded DNS on networks you create yourself.

code:
$ docker run -d --name catalog-db \
  --network northbridge-net \
  -v catalog-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:16

$ docker run -d --name catalog \
  --network northbridge-net \
  -p 8080:3000 \
  northbridge/catalog:1.5
caption: --network stacks with -v and -p on the same docker run command -- nothing about those earlier flags changes.

code:
$ docker exec catalog ping -c 1 catalog-db
PING catalog-db (172.18.0.2): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 172.18.0.2: icmp_seq=0 ttl=64 time=0.071 ms
caption: Docker's embedded DNS, active only on user-defined networks, maps catalog-db's name to wherever its current IP actually is.
